corrected_atomic_success.interpretation: Only a complete rendered snapshot is moved onto the final path.

corrected_temporary_failure.interpretation: Rendering to a same-directory temporary file and deleting it on failure preserves the prior target and leaves no partial publication.

former_direct_target_failure.interpretation: Writing the rendered PNG directly to the final path can destroy a previous validated artifact when rendering fails after truncation.

findings.detail: _emit_quantitative passes the final figure path directly to savefig; a failed render can truncate or partially replace prior evidence.
The quantitative PNG is not rendered to retained temporary bytes and atomically published to the final target.
The matplotlib figure is closed only after savefig returns; a render exception can bypass cleanup in long registry builds.

primary_software_references.statement_supported: If successful, replacement is atomic; keeping the temporary file in the target directory avoids a cross-filesystem move.
mkstemp securely creates the temporary file and requires explicit cleanup.
savefig writes to the supplied path or file-like object; an explicit format can decouple rendering format from a temporary filename suffix.

repository_observation.current_cleanup: plt.close(fig) occurs only after savefig returns
repository_observation.evidence_scope: The executable audit input is an exact connector-reconstructed function excerpt; the Git blob identifies the full current file.

required_remediation.cleanup: Close the matplotlib figure in a finally block so render errors cannot leak figure resources across a registry build.
required_remediation.publication: Atomically publish the retained render snapshot to the final path with flush, fsync, os.replace, cleanup, and final-target digest verification.
required_remediation.regression: Inject save and replacement failures and prove that a pre-existing validated target remains byte-identical and no temporary file remains.
required_remediation.render: Render each quantitative PNG to a same-directory temporary file with an explicit PNG format, then read and retain the complete bytes.

scientific_boundary: This audit validates quantitative figure-publication integrity only. It does not validate any plotted scientific value, uncertainty, calibration, PID, timing, stopping profile, pile-up rate, or detector-performance claim.
unrun_checks: scientific regeneration of any plotted quantity
